name: PT Garda Tujuh Buana Tbk

frontmatter.title: Garda Tujuh Buana — a sub-scale, deep-discount coal miner whose equity sits behind a tax claim
frontmatter.summary: GTBO is a sub-scale, low-calorie coal miner restarting under an approved RKAB. The mine's operating value is below the 16.5 million-dollar tax payable, so the base case is Rp0. The probability-weighted value is Rp76; after the 30.0% liquidity discount the target is Rp53, bull-dominated at a 20.0% weight. We initiate at SELL (total return -68.6%).
thesis: GTBO's product is a deep-discount grade: the director put it at about 3,000 kcal/kg, below Indonesia's domestic minimum, so it is priced at roughly 30.0% of Newcastle and sits at the bottom of the grade ladder [S11]. In 2025 its sales split 60.0% to the Thai exporter Asia Green Energy and 40.0% to the local buyer PT Niaga Energi Dunia, so it is not an export-only book [S7].

The 2026 RKAB was approved only on 25 September 2026 at 818 kt, and mining restarted in the first half of October; management guides 400 kt to 500 kt by December, so the year is a one-quarter stub [S2]. We run the approved ceiling of 0.82 Mt thereafter, not the 1.5 Mt of 2022 or the unfulfilled 2.6 Mt plan for 2023 [S11][S15].

The balance sheet drives the call. The 30 June 2026 accounts carry a tax payable of 16.5 million dollars against equity of 22.9 million and negligible cash; that claim ranks ahead of shareholders and is not in the data pack's debt line [S0][S7]. At the deck's through-cycle price the mine's operating value of US$5.8m is below the claim, so the base-case equity is worth nothing.

The margin is razor thin. At our realised price of 35.4 dollars a tonne the FY2023 cost ratios — 19.0 dollars of direct mining and logistics, 5.0% royalty and 33.0% overhead — leave EBITDA of US$2.4m on 0.82 Mt [S0][S2].

The market is pricing the restart, an RKAB restoration and a tax settlement, not the through-cycle base. Our reverse cash flow says today's price implies a Newcastle benchmark of about 168.4 dollars a tonne, above the 150.3 spot print [S0]. The bull state restores the RKAB to the 1.5 Mt the company held in 2022 and narrows the grade discount, and it carries essentially the whole weighted target of Rp76; the full tax claim is still charged inside it, so a settlement is additional upside not in the number [S2][S7].

catalysts.event: Annual general meeting — approval of the FY2025 accounts and a change of directors and commissioners
Nine-month 2026 financial statements and any update on the tax assessment
FY2026 audited results and the 2027 RKAB application

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of PT Garda Tujuh Buana Tbk at SELL with a twelve-month target of Rp53 against a last price of Rp170, a total return of -68.6% [S0]. The call is not a judgement on the coal cycle, where our house deck is neutral on thermal coal. It is a judgement on a sub-scale, deep-discount mine whose restart is real but whose equity is subordinated to a tax claim the quoted price does not appear to discount [S7].

The variant view is about *what the market is capitalising*. GTBO is a single-mine producer on Bunyu Island whose coal is a low-calorie grade at the bottom of the price ladder; in 2025 about 60.0% of sales went to a Thai exporter and 40.0% to a local buyer [S7][S11]. Our base case runs the approved 818 kt RKAB at a realisation of 30.0% of Newcastle, direct cost of 19.0 dollars a tonne plus overheads, and the regulation royalty, which produces EBITDA of US$2.4m in the first full year [S2][S0]. That is a real but marginal business at through-cycle prices: the operating value of the DCF is US$5.8m [S0].

The balance-sheet claim is the whole story. The 30 June 2026 accounts carry a tax payable of 16.5 million dollars and total liabilities of 22.4 million against equity of 22.9 million, and the same accounts charged a 4.6 million-dollar tax assessment through other expenses [S7]. The data pack's debt line shows only the small bank borrowing, so the tax payable sits outside the modelled net debt; we carry it as a negative bridge item because it ranks ahead of shareholders and is not captured anywhere else in the cash flow [S7][S0]. Because the operating value is below the claim, the base-case equity value rounds to Rp0 a share. That is the base case, not the target.

The target is the probability-weighted value, and it is bull-dominated. The base and bear states are both worth Rp0 after the claim; the bull state, with the RKAB restored and a narrower grade discount, is worth Rp382. The weighted value is Rp76, and the house 30.0% liquidity discount takes the published target to Rp53. The target sits below the Rp170 price because the state that clears the price carries only a 20.0% weight; doubling that weight at the expense of the base state would raise the target but still leave it below the quoted price, so the SELL does not rest on the weighting [S0]. What moves the value, in order: the resolution of the tax claim, the size of the annual RKAB, and the coal price. A settlement at a fraction of the booked payable, or an RKAB restored to the levels the company held in 2022, would each move the equity materially; so would a sustained spot price. Our reverse cash flow puts the market's implied Newcastle benchmark at about 168.4 dollars a tonne, above the 150.3 spot print, which is the most bullish assumption embedded in the price [S0]. We argue that is not the most likely through-cycle marker, and the valuation tables show the sensitivity.

PT Garda Tujuh Buana Tbk is an Indonesian thermal-coal producer whose mine sits in the unpopulated north-central part of Bunyu Island, Bulungan Regency, in what is now North Kalimantan [S10]. The company was founded in 1996, listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in 2009 and describes itself as producing low-ash, low-sulphur thermal coal for coal-fired power plants in both domestic and export markets [S10]. In practice the product has been a low-calorie coal sold mostly for export: the director told Kontan that the coal is about 3,000 kcal/kg, below the domestic minimum, and the company's 2023 plan was to export all of its volume to buyers in China, Thailand, India and later Vietnam [S11]. In 2025 it sold 60.0% of its volume through the Thai exporter Asia Green Energy Public Co Ltd and 40.0% to the local buyer PT Niaga Energi Dunia, so the book is mostly export but not export-only [S7]. A 2017 report put the calorific value higher, at 4,800 kcal/kg to 5,100 kcal/kg, and we flag that inconsistency rather than resolve it; the more recent director statement is the one the model uses [S14][S11].

The operating model is contractor-led. GTBO uses PT VPR Laxmindo as its mining contractor, and the contractor relationship is the reason the company's own sustaining capital has been negligible [S14][S0]. The company runs a single mine and a single product line; there are no reported segments, no smelter, no logistics division and no other revenue [S10]. Its customers are few and disclosed by name: in 2025 the exporter Asia Green Energy Public Co Ltd accounted for 60.0% of sales and the local buyer PT Niaga Energi Dunia for 40.0% [S7]. That is a concentrated book in a business where the product is a commodity and the buyer can switch origin easily [S7][S10].

The strategy, as far as the record shows, is simply to keep the Bunyu mine running within the annual RKAB. There is no growth project, no acquisition and no downstream plan in the archived disclosure [S10][S2]. The 2026 plan is to produce 400 kt to 500 kt after the RKAB was approved on 25 September 2026 and mining restarted in the first half of October [S2]. The company is a price-taking challenger in a market dominated by the large Indonesian producers, and its sub-scale output and low grade are the two facts that shape the economics [S2][S11].

Control is highly concentrated. At 30 September 2021 the register showed DBS Bank Ltd-SG with 33.4%, Bank Julius Baer and Co. Ltd with 32.8%, PT Garda Minerals with 26.2% and the public with 7.6% [S16]. The pack's insider figure of 94.5% and free float of 7.6% are consistent with that register [S0]. Two of the three large holders are private banks, which on IDX usually act as nominee or pledge accounts; the archived record does not identify the beneficial owners behind them, and we treat that opacity as a governance fact rather than speculate [S16].

Garda Tujuh Buana is one of the older small coal names on the Indonesian exchange and has spent much of
its listed life either suspended, on a special board or negotiating a restart. Its concession is on an
island with no domestic power demand, so the mine has always depended on barging coal to export buyers
rather than selling into the domestic market. That structure explains why its fortunes track the export
price for low-grade coal rather than the domestic electricity market.

Indonesia is the world's largest thermal-coal exporter and the annual RKAB is the supply lever. The Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources expected about 720 Mt of national coal production under the 2026 RKAB, with almost all applications approved by late September 2026 [S21]. For a small producer the RKAB is not a formality: GTBO's 2026 application went through four rounds of evaluation because of technical documents, supporting permits and administrative completeness, and the delay is the direct cause of the nil sales in the first half of the year [S2][S7] [S21][S2][S7].

The price backdrop is a two-speed market. The house coal deck carries Newcastle at 137.0 dollars a tonne for 2026, 118.0 for 2027 and a long-run anchor of 105.0, against a spot print of 150.3; the high-GAR HBA is set at 112.0 for 2027 (fund record). The gap between spot and the through-cycle marker is the war-premium carry the desk does not expect to persist, and it matters more than usual here because the stock's implied price assumes a level above the spot print lasts [S0]. The macro desk's tilt on thermal coal is neutral, in a balance-of-payments-pressure regime (KB, 24 October 2026).

The grade ladder is the competitive fact that matters for GTBO. The reviewed deck carries HBA III for low-calorie GAR coal at a spot of 45.5 dollars a tonne against Newcastle's 150.3 — a ratio of about 30.0%. GTBO's stated grade is below that tranche, so its realised price sits at the bottom of the ladder [S11] (fund record). That is not a temporary discount; it is the structural position of a low-calorie, high-ash product in a market where buyers price calorific value, ash and sulphur directly [S11].

On the five-forces view the industry is unattractive for a sub-scale price taker. Supplier power is low for labour but high for the mining contractor and for barging, buyer power is high because the product is homogeneous and the customer list is two names, the threat of substitutes is real in the power market through gas and renewables, and rivalry is intense because Indonesian RKAB volumes clear into the same seaborne market [S7][S21]. Barriers to entry are the permit, not the capital. GTBO's only durable asset is the mine and its RKAB; there is no cost-curve moat, no logistics moat and no customer lock-in that the record discloses [S10][S2].

Regulation cuts both ways. The determined export price floor and the DMO framework shape realisations and the royalty band, while the annual RKAB sets the ceiling. GTBO's licence is an IUP and the product's 3,000 kcal/kg puts it in the up-to-4,200 kcal/kg GAR tranche of the open-pit schedule; its reference grade, HBA III, is 45.5 dollars a tonne, below the first HBA threshold, so the applicable royalty is 5.0% of revenue, not the upper band (PP 19/2025, deck table coal.royalty_iup_low; [S2]). The domestic power price cap is inert here: only 40.0% of 2025 sales were local, to a non-power buyer, and the realised price sits far below the 70.0-dollar cap, so no tonne is priced at the cap [S7][S11].

The published record is a collapse followed by a stub. Revenue fell from US$58.8m in FY2023 to US$27.3m in FY2024 and US$10.0m in FY2025, while cost of goods sold stayed at US$15.2m in FY2025 — a gross loss, with gross profit of US$-5.2m [S0]. The first half of 2026 was worse: nil sales against 1.3 million dollars of cost of goods still running and 1.6 million of operating expenses and a 4.6 million-dollar tax assessment, which together produced the loss the filing records [S7]. The company has not sold a tonne since the fourth quarter of 2025 [S0][S7].

Our forecast restarts the mine in the fourth quarter of 2026 and runs the approved ceiling thereafter. Volume is 0.45 Mt in FY2026E, the one-quarter stub, and 0.82 Mt from FY2027E — the 818 kt RKAB, held flat [S2]. At the deck's Newcastle path and a realisation of 30.0%, revenue is US$18.5m in FY2026E and US$29.0m in FY2027E, with EBITDA of US$2.9m and US$2.4m respectively [S0]. The cost build is 19.0 dollars a tonne of direct mining and logistics, US$9.6m of overheads at 33.0% of revenue and US$1.5m of royalty at 5.0% [S0][S2].

The cost ratio is the swing factor, and we anchor it on the last full operating year. FY2023 carried cost of goods sold of US$33.4m and operating expenses of US$19.4m on US$58.8m of revenue — a combined cost that consumed almost all of the revenue [S0]. At the 1.5 Mt 2022 RKAB and the 2.6 Mt planned for 2023, those costs bracket a per-tonne total that contains our FY2027E build; at the smaller 2026 ceiling the fixed-cost drag per tonne is higher, which is why we carry the 33.0% overhead ratio rather than the lower ratio of the shutdown year [S0][S15]. The result is a thin but positive EBITDA at through-cycle prices, not the wider margin the earlier cost base implied.

The cash-flow and balance-sheet picture is the constraint. Operating cash flow turned negative in FY2025 as sales collapsed and capital expenditure was negligible, consistent with the contractor model [S0][S14]. Cash was negligible at 30 June 2026, and net debt is close to zero, but the tax payable of 16.5 million dollars is the effective financing issue [S7][S0]. The FY2026E cash flow includes a one-off working-capital release as the shutdown inventory unwinds to a 10.0%-of-revenue ratio — the delta is -2.4 million dollars, a source of cash; that ratio is held thereafter, so the release does not repeat, and it is disclosed here rather than left as an unexplained boost [S0]. We model no dividend: the company has paid one cash dividend in the pack's history and none since, the trailing dividend yield is 0.0%, and distributing cash ahead of the tax claim is not the most-likely path [S0][S7].

Earnings quality is poor and the record is thin. The accruals screen is not meaningful on a company with almost no revenue, but two flags are material. First, the gap between the reported loss and cash: the FY2025 net loss, with net profit of US$-7.8m, against a negative operating cash flow is explained by the shutdown and by working capital, not by a cash-generative business [S0]. Second, the tax assessment and the jump in the tax payable to 16.5 million dollars are a balance-sheet event the market can see but the pack's debt line does not capture [S7]. The FY2025 accounts were signed only on 15 July 2026, which is why the annual meeting is being held in November [S6]. We have not restated the pack's revenue or cost lines because no archived source contradicts them; what the pack lacks is a volume series, which we discuss in the valuation section [S0][S7][S6].

The right method for a single-mine coal producer is a life-of-asset DCF at through-cycle prices, with the balance sheet taken off at the end. We use the deck's Newcastle path (118.0 dollars a tonne in 2027, 105.0 in 2029 and a long-run anchor of 105.0) and a realisation of 30.0% [S11] (fund record). The realisation is a grade judgement, not a fitted last-actual ratio: the archive has no FY2025 tonnage and FY2025 was a shutdown. It is anchored on the observed HBA III/Newcastle relationship in the reviewed deck and cross-checked against the one actual tonnage the record discloses — 0.11 Mt sold for US$4.1m in the two months of 2021 production (F17, F18) — and against the FY2023 revenue line at the RKAB/plan volume bracket [S15]. The applied ladder is:

| Step | Value | |---|---| | Newcastle FY2027E benchmark | 118.0 | | Grade realisation applied | 30.0% | | GTBO realised price FY2027E | 35.4 | | HBA III spot (3,400 kcal/kg GAR) | 45.5 | | Newcastle spot | 150.3 |

The DCF ends where cumulative value stops adding, so the horizon is a working-mine life rather than a terminal-growth perpetuity [S0]. There is no reserve statement in the archived record: the only reserve-adjacent disclosure is the RKAB production ceiling, and the company's own profile and site material is silent on reserves and resources [S4][S10]. The horizon is therefore an explicit judgment, not a reserve life. The DCF's present value is concentrated in the first full years (the table below falls away sharply after them), so a shorter life would reduce the value and a longer one would add little at these prices; we treat the life as a downside sensitivity rather than a reserve-derived input.

The cost of capital build is 10.4% at the weighted-average level, from a cost of equity of 10.5%, a risk-free rate of 5.0%, an equity risk premium of 4.2%, a country premium of 2.5% and a levered beta of 0.81 [S0]. The low debt weight reflects a company that has historically funded itself and has almost no borrowings; the beta is the industry median from the desk's regression set [S0].

The primary method gives an enterprise value of US$5.8m. We do not use an exit multiple: there is no comparable transaction for a sub-scale, low-calorie Indonesian mine whose only listed peers are much larger and higher-grade, and a terminal multiple would capitalise the current price rather than the asset. The cross-checks are therefore secondary. The pack's history-multiple table shows the shares at 0.56 times FY2025 book, but the book has since fallen from 41.8 million at end-2025 to 22.9 million at 30 June 2026 [S0][S7]. Against a market capitalisation of IDR425.0bn, the shares are at rather than below current book before the tax claim is deducted, and the claim absorbs most of that book: the apparent discount to the older book has gone. On our FY2027E numbers the modelled P/E is 14.65 and EV/EBITDA 9.35, both pre-claim [S0]. The dividend-yield cross-check is unavailable because we model no dividend [S0].

The bridge is where the call is made. The DCF's enterprise value of US$5.8m less the net debt on the balance sheet at 30 June 2026 — the net debt line the DCF table above deducts, struck on the latest reported balance sheet, not the FY2026E forecast line of US$-0.1m, which is a forecast year and shows net cash — gives an equity value before the tax claim that is itself small; the 16.5 million-dollar tax payable, carried as a negative item, then takes the base-case equity to Rp0 a share [S0][S7]. This is not double counting: the pack's balance-sheet debt and cash exclude tax liabilities, and our cash-flow forecast does not model the payment of the existing payable, so the bridge is the only place the claim is charged [S0][S7]. The booked payable is the balance-sheet amount; the 1H26 accounts also charged a 4.6 million-dollar SKP through other expenses, and under UU KUP Article 13 the shortfall carries administrative interest, historically 2.0% a month for a maximum of 24 months [S22]. The booked amount is therefore a floor, not a cap. We charge the FY2026E-only assessment in the profit and loss as a one-off and do not repeat it [S7].

The reverse cash flow is the disciplining check, and its mechanics matter. Holding volume at the RKAB and the full tax claim constant, today's price implies a Newcastle benchmark of about 168.4 dollars a tonne — a factor of 1.43 on our FY2027E marker and above the 150.3 spot print [S0] (fund record). In other words, the market is paying for a price level above the war-premium spot to persist, not for the deck's mean-reverting path. The solve is single-variable and therefore not unique: a price built on RKAB restoration or a tax settlement would imply a lower coal marker, and the bull state is the model's test of that combination [S2][S7]. The conclusion that the price embeds a spot-level-or-higher coal marker survives only on base volume and the full claim, and we state it that way.

At the top of the sensitivity grid the base-case equity remains a fraction of the quoted price, and the value response is one-sided at these costs: it becomes material only when the benchmark is pushed well above the deck's path. Running the model at the spot print rather than the deck path still leaves the base case short of the price on base volume — that is the NAV-at-spot check — so the quoted price needs the bull state's volume and price together. The target is nevertheless bull-dominated: the base and bear states are worth Rp0 after the claim, so essentially the whole probability-weighted value of Rp76 comes from the bull state at weight 20.0%. Doubling that weight at the expense of the base state raises the weighted value and the discounted target, but not to the quoted price; we therefore do not rely on the weighting to produce the SELL.

The main modelling caveat is volume history. GTBO does not disclose a tonnage series in the archived record; the pack carries revenue and cost lines but no volume, and the press record gives tonnage only for the 2021 restart and the RKAB levels [S15]. The engine's calibration gate therefore cannot re-price FY2025A at a volume it does not have, and we justify that in the QC record rather than invent a number. Calibration is anchored on the FY2023 operating year and on the revenue line instead, and the report states the resulting gap openly [S0][S7].

The first risk is the tax claim. A 16.5 million-dollar payable against 22.9 million of equity is material in any outcome; if it is paid in full and on demand, the company needs cash it does not have (cash was negligible at the half year) or an asset sale that is not in the record [S7][S0]. The booked payable excludes the Article 13 administrative-interest sanction on the active assessment: historically 2.0% a month for up to 24 months [S22], so the maximum exposure is the booked amount plus that sanction, not the booked amount alone. Likelihood high, impact high. A negotiated settlement, a reversal or a waiver of the sanction would be a material upside, but it is not the bull case: the bull's core driver is restoration of the RKAB to the level the company held in 2022, and every modelled state charges the claim in full, so a settlement at a fraction of book sits on top of the bull value as upside we do not capture [S7][S22].

The second is funding. With negligible cash, a 16.5 million-dollar payable and a restart that needs working capital, a rights issue, placement or asset sale is a plausible route; none is disclosed in the record and no funding commitment from the controlling holders appears in it [S5][S6]. We do not model dilution in the base or bull: a placement at the market price is broadly value-neutral per share, and an issue at a discount transfers value only if the stock trades below intrinsic value; the bear state is already floored at Rp0, so dilution on top of a worthless equity cannot lower the target further. It remains a real downside for holders who buy at today's price, and it is a signpost to watch [S5][S6].

The third is permitting and volume. The 2026 RKAB was approved only after four evaluation rounds and at the 818 kt ceiling; a repeat of the delay would again stop production, as it did in the first half of 2026 [S2][S7]. Likelihood medium, impact high. The fourth is price and grade: a low-calorie product has no pricing power, and a wider discount as buyers screen for calorific value would compress the already thin spread between 35.4 dollars of realised price and 19.0 dollars of direct cost [S11][S0]. Likelihood medium, impact high [S11].

The fifth is liquidity and governance. The free float is 7.6%, three holders own almost all of the register, the shares trade about IDR29.9m a day and there were dozens of zero-volume days in the last quarter [S0][S16]. The stock has a history of suspensions: it was halted in 2020-22 and threatened with delisting, halted again in July 2026 for a late quarterly report, and resumed in September [S16][S20][S18]. A holder may not be able to exit at the quoted price; that is why the house applies a liquidity discount to the target [S0].

The final risk is operational and ESG: a single mine, a single contractor, a mine on an island with no domestic power demand, and a product sold mostly to export buyers with a local minority. A contractor dispute or a barge/logistics interruption has no diversification buffer [S14][S10]. The environmental exposure is conventional for coal — land disturbance, dust and water — and the company discloses no rehabilitation provision detail in the record we can source [S10].

The scenarios mirror the same three drivers. In the bear case the RKAB is renewed near the 2026 guidance low rather than the approved ceiling, the grade discount widens and the tax claim is paid in full including the Article 13 sanction; the equity is worth Rp0, because the claim already absorbs the operating value at this price. In the base case the approved ceiling holds and the claim is charged in full; the equity is worth Rp0. In the bull case the RKAB is restored to the 1.5 Mt level of 2022, the grade discount narrows, and the equity is worth Rp382; the claim is still charged in full, so a settlement at a fraction is additional upside [S2][S15][S7]. The probabilities are 0.50 base, 0.30 bear and 0.20 bull [S0].

The signposts that would change the view: an announced settlement of the tax case, a 2027 RKAB materially above the 2026 ceiling, a return to profitability in the quarterly accounts, and any corporate action that brings new equity or an asset sale. A sustained Newcastle price at the spot level would also move us toward the bull case, but we would want to see it in the company's realised price before capitalising it [S2][S7].

Ownership is the defining governance fact. At the last register disclosed, three holders — DBS Bank Ltd-SG, Bank Julius Baer and Co. Ltd and PT Garda Minerals — held 33.4%, 32.8% and 26.2% respectively, with 7.6% in public hands [S16]. The pack's insider figure of 94.5% differs slightly from that register; we use the disclosed stakes as the sourced number and treat the pack's figure as its own [S0][S16]. The company does not disclose the beneficial owners behind the two bank holdings in the archived record; we treat that as an opacity flag, not an allegation. The free float is below the exchange's minimum, which is why the new notation regime matters for the name [S8][S9][S16].

Board and management are in flux. The annual meeting called for 18 November 2026 will seek approval of the FY2025 accounts, a change of directors that replaces Mastan Singh with Ganesh Tikamdas Ramchandani and Pasi Ajay Chhotelal, and a change of commissioner that replaces Sandeep Kaur with Timothy James Cornelius as independent commissioner [S6]. The FY2025 accounts were signed on 15 July 2026, so the annual meeting itself is late and the company is seeking a dispensation [S6]. That is a disclosure discipline flag, not a fraud finding [S6].

The company has a history of shareholder conflict and suspension. A 2012 extraordinary meeting was disputed by the then-president commissioner, who said his shares had been transferred without his consent and that the meeting was invalid [S17]. The stock was suspended for more than two years and faced a delisting threat in 2022 [S16]; it was placed on the special monitoring board in September 2023 and removed in October 2023 [S19]; it was suspended again in July 2026 for failing to file its first-quarter report and resumed in September [S20][S7]. These are optics-and-structure flags, not evidence of fabricated cash, but they go to the reliability of the disclosure and to exit risk [S16][S19][S20].

The dividend record is thin: one cash dividend in the pack's history and none since, with a trailing yield of 0.0% [S0]. The auditor and opinion are not in the archived record we could source, and we do not assert one; the accounts' late signature is the only audit-related fact we can cite [S6]. On ESG, the company is a conventional coal miner with the usual land, dust and water exposures; no rehabilitation provision, emissions target or climate transition plan appears in the sourced material [S10]. We do not score it beyond that [S0][S6].

The dated catalysts are the annual meeting on 18 November 2026, the nine-month 2026 financial statements due by the end of November, and the FY2026 audited results and 2027 RKAB application in the first quarter of 2027 [S6][S7][S2]. The first two will show whether the restart has produced cash and whether the tax payable has moved; the third will set the volume for our forecast year [S2][S6][S7].

Between updates we watch four KPIs: the quarterly coal sales volume against the 818 kt RKAB, the realised price against the Newcastle benchmark, the cash cost per tonne against our 19.0-dollar assumption, and the tax payable and any settlement disclosure [S2][S0][S7]. A fifth, the free float and any new notation, is a governance monitor rather than a value driver [S8][S9] [S2][S0][S7].

We will also monitor the coal deck. The house marker for Newcastle is 118.0 dollars a tonne for 2027 against a spot of 150.3, and the through-cycle anchor is 105.0; a deck revision that lifts the long-run marker would change our valuation more than any single quarter's result (fund record). The stock's implied price is already close to the spot level, so the asymmetry in the deck is toward our base case, not away from it [S0].

valuation.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)
Dividend yield
valuation.basis: no dividend expected in the next 12 months — a yield valuation does not apply

bear.narrative: The RKAB is renewed near the 2026 guidance low of 0.45 Mt rather than the 0.82 Mt ceiling, the grade discount widens as Chinese and Indian buyers screen out 3,000 kcal coal, and the restart needs new money - a rights issue or placement at a deep discount - because the US$16.5m tax claim absorbs the cash the mine generates. At this volume and price the equity is worthless before dilution, so dilution adds no further value loss to a floored base.

bull.narrative: The 2027 RKAB is restored to the 1.5 Mt the company held in 2022 (F16) rather than the unfulfilled 2.6 Mt plan, and the grade sells at a narrower discount as power-plant demand for low-CV coal recovers. The tax payable is still charged in full in this state: a settlement at a fraction of book is additional upside that the bull value does not contain.

assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 0.45 Mt: the 2026 RKAB was approved only on 25 September 2026 for 817,900 tonnes, and management guides production of 400-500 kt by December with mining restarting in the first or second week of October (S2, F1-F4), so only about one quarter of a full year is available; the midpoint of the guided range is used. FY2027E onward 0.82 Mt: the approved 2026 RKAB ceiling is the only current, sourced production authority; we hold it flat rather than assuming a re-rating to the 1.5 Mt (2022) or 2.6 Mt (2023 plan) levels, because the 2023 plan was never delivered and the company's own 2026 guidance is half of it (S11, S15, F15-F16). The volume history is not disclosed in the archived record, so the engine cannot re-price the FY2025 shutdown year; that gap is explained in qc_justifications.calibration.unavailable and in section 4.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: 0.30x Newcastle, a grade judgment, not a last-actual calibration. The company states its coal is 3,000 cal/gram (F14, a 2022 director statement), far below the 4,200 kcal/kg boundary of the low-calorie tranche, so it is a deep-discount product, not a Newcastle grade. The ratio is the observed grade relationship in the reviewed deck at the latest print: HBA III (3,400 kcal/kg GAR) spot of 45.53 USD/t over Newcastle spot of 150.35 USD/t is 0.303 (fund record). It is cross-checked against the one actual tonnage the archive discloses: in the two months of production after the 2021 restart the company sold 107,370 t for US$4.11m (F17, F18), an average of US$38.3/t, and the model's FY2027E ASP (0.30 x the deck's 118.0 newc) sits at US$35.4/t, inside the US$30-39/t range implied by the FY2021 actual and the FY2023 revenue of US$58.8m over the 1.5-1.8 Mt the 2022 RKAB and 2023 plan bracket (F15, F16). No FY2025 volume exists in the archive, so the ratio is not fitted to that shutdown year. It is held flat; the grade wedge widens inside the bear's price leg rather than being assumed away.

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: Zero. In 2025 sales split 60% to the Thai exporter Asia Green Energy and 40% to the local buyer PT Niaga Energi Dunia (F5, S7), so the product is not export-only. The DMO cap, however, applies to coal sold to domestic power plants; the local buyer is not a DMO power offtaker in the record, and the realised price (about 0.30 x newc, well under US$70/t) sits below the cap level, so even a capped tonne would not be re-priced down. No tonne is therefore exposed to the cap.

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0 as a cost-intensity factor, not a physical strip ratio: no stripping ratio is disclosed in the archived record, so the whole cash cost is carried in cost_per_bcm and other_cost_unit per tonne rather than inventing a stripping number. Strip-ratio drift is not modelled because no mine plan or strip history is available to source it.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: 13.0 USD/t of mining and hauling cost at the 0.82 Mt plan volume, plus 6.0 USD/t of logistics in other_cost_unit. The arithmetic behind it: FY2023 revenue of US$58.8m carried cost of goods sold of US$33.4m and operating expenses of US$19.4m (pack, S0); at the 1.5-1.8 Mt scale implied by the 2022 RKAB of 1.5 Mt and the 2023 plan of 2.6 Mt (F15, F16), COGS per tonne was US$19-22 and total cost US$29-35/t. Our 19 USD/t of direct mining plus logistics sits at the low end of the COGS range and, with the 33% overhead ratio below and 5% royalty, gives a total cost of about US$32/t - inside the FY2023 range and appropriately above the per-tonne COGS because the 0.82 Mt RKAB is roughly half the scale the company ran in 2023, so fixed overhead is spread over fewer tonnes. The old 18% overhead ratio is discarded: it was taken from the 2025 shutdown year and understated the 33-36% opex ratio the FY2022-FY2024 operating years actually carried (S0). The contractor structure (S14, F26) keeps sustaining capital light. This is the central uncertainty in the model and is treated as such in the scenarios and section 5; no cost inflation is assumed beyond the deck's USD escalation.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: Zero at the model level because diesel sits inside the contractor's mining rate (S14, F26).

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: 6.0 USD/t for barging, transshipment and processing beyond the contractor's mining rate. GTBO ships from Bunyu Island through barge and transshipment to export customers in Thailand, China and India (S15), and the 2022-23 revenue-per-tonne of roughly US$31-35 against a low-grade product leaves little room for a higher logistics wedge. Held flat in real terms across the forecast.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: 5%, the IUP open-pit low-calorie band for HBA below US$70/t (PP 19/2025, deck table coal.royalty_iup_low). Licence IUP is stated in params; the product's 3,000 cal/gram puts it in the up-to-4,200 kcal/kg GAR tranche, and its reference grade HBA III is US$45.53/t, below the first threshold, so the band rate is 5% for the forecast. Reading the high-GAR HBA (US$112/t) into the schedule, as the prior draft did, wrongly selected the 9% upper band; no LK effective rate is disclosed in the archive, so the regulation band is the sourced rate. Held flat through the forecast; a coal spike that lifted HBA III above US$70 would add one point of royalty.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: No other revenue is disclosed; the company is a single-mine coal seller (S10).

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: Engine default; other revenue is zero.

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: 0.40 USD/t. The pack carries property, plant and equipment of only US$0.15m at 30 June 2026 (S0) and no depreciation line, consistent with a contractor-operated, largely depreciated mine; the charge is kept small rather than assumed away, and the pack's missing D&A is not used to flatter cash earnings.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: 0.25 USD/t, a real allowance but far below the prior 1.0 USD/t. Pack capex was US$0.018m in FY2025 and US$0.001m in FY2023 (S0) — negligible because the mine is contractor-operated (S14, F26), which is why no mine plan sources a higher sustaining spend. The prior 1.0 USD/t was unsourced, about 50x the FY2025 actual per tonne, and against the corrected cost base it exceeded the mine's late-life EBITDA; 0.25 USD/t is still several times the last actual and does not assume zero capital forever.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: No expansion project is disclosed in the archived record (S2, S10).

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: 10% of revenue, the ratio the operating years carried before the shutdown: FY2022 net working capital was US$4.88m on US$49.27m of revenue (S0), FY2024 US$1.75m on US$27.25m, and FY2023 was a small negative. FY2025's 42% is a shutdown artefact (US$10.0m of revenue against US$4.2m of working capital). Using 10% holds a real operating working capital at the restart and does not assume it away. The tax payable of US$16.50m (S7, F10) is a claim, not operating capital, and is carried in the valuation bridge, not here. The FY2026E cash flow still shows a one-off release as the shutdown inventory unwinds to the 10% ratio; that release is disclosed in section 4 and is not repeated, because the ratio is held thereafter.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: 22% statutory corporate rate applied to positive pre-tax profit. The historical effective rate is unusable (loss years carried zero tax; FY2023 was 24%, FY2022 2% on a one-off), so the statutory rate is the most-likely convention.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 9.2%, the FY2023-25 average interest rate on the small outstanding debt (pack, S0).

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 0% — cash was US$0.04m at 30 June 2026 (S0), immaterial to the valuation.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No new borrowing is disclosed; the company has historically funded itself and the tax payable is carried in the bridge, not as debt (S15, S7).

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: 0.0 from FY2027E. The FY2026E line carries the US$4.56m SKP tax assessment charged in 1H26 (S7, F9), which is a one-off and is not repeated; it is also carried as a claim in the valuation bridge.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: No minority interest in the pack balance sheet (S0).

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: 0.0. GTBO paid one dividend (FY2023) and has paid nothing since; dps_ttm is zero (S0), the 30 June 2026 balance sheet has US$0.04m of cash against a US$16.50m tax payable (S0, S7, F10) and no revenue in 1H26. Distributing cash ahead of that liability is not the most-likely path; any dividend is upside to the bull case, not the base.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No rights issue or placement is disclosed; 2,500m shares (S0).

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House USD terminal growth of 2% (deck); the DCF life cut-off, not terminal growth, sets the end of the mine's value.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 33% of revenue, the ratio the last full operating year carried: FY2023 opex was US$19.4m on US$58.8m of revenue (32.9%), FY2024 36.0% and FY2022 33.3% (S0). The prior 18% was taken from the 2025 shutdown year (US$1.5m on US$10.0m, 15%) and understated the cost base the operating years actually ran; it is reversed here as unsourced caution in the wrong direction. At the 0.82 Mt plan the proportionally-applied 33% still understates the fixed-cost drag (a lower volume spreads the same overhead over fewer tonnes), so it is not an aggressive setting. Inside the model's 0-50% guardrail; the sensitivity shows the effect of a swing.

challenges.challenge: F14 is labelled FY2025A but its own locator is "Kontan, 14 Dec 2022" (S11), and the report states the company "exported all of its volume" and "every tonne is exported" while its own F5 (S7, Sep 2026) shows 40% of 2025 sales were local to PT Niaga Energi Dunia. The export-only premise that sets capped_share to zero is not supported for the last actual year. (The US$70 DMO cap is above the ~US$35/t realised price, so the value effect may be nil, but the facts and the DMO sentence are wrong.)
challenges.answer: F14 is relabelled FY2022A and sourced to the 2022 Kontan interview; section 1 now separates the 2023 all-export plan (S11) from the 2025 60/40 export/local actual (F5/F31, S7); the DMO paragraph rests on the actual customer mix and the realised price being far below the cap, not on an export-only premise. assumptions.capped_share basis rewritten the same way.

challenges.challenge: Realisation 0.30 is claimed "calibrated on the last actual", but no FY2025 volume exists; the "~0.3 Mt implied volume" is itself derived from 0.30 x 108.4 x 0.3 Mt = US$9.8m, so the calibration is circular and cannot fail. The 0.30 is really the spot HBA III/newc ratio, not a last-actual calibration.
challenges.answer: 0.30 is now labelled a grade judgment read from HBA III over Newcastle at the latest print, not a last-actual calibration; the archive has no FY2025 tonnage and FY2025 was a shutdown. It is cross-checked against the one actual tonnage (107,370 t for US$4.11m, F17/F18) and the FY2023 revenue bracket (F15/F16); the circular implied-volume argument is removed.

challenges.challenge: Royalty: the engine reads d.coal.hba (112, >90 band) for a 3,000 kcal product, but the deck's own table is by HBA band and this grade's HBA III is 45.53 ( 5%), not 9%. No LK effective royalty rate is cited. The price marker is also Newcastle although the commodity card says coal realises off HBA/ICI.
challenges.answer: Royalty accepted: the engine now reads the 5% IUP open-pit low-calorie band (HBA III 45.53 below the 70 threshold) from PP 19/2025 rather than the 9% high-GAR band, and no LK effective rate exists in the archive - the report says so. The Newcastle marker is retained because the deck's HBA III series is spot-only with no forecast path; the HBA III relationship is carried in the 0.30 realisation and the ladder table shows the royalty as money and rate.

challenges.challenge: The life-of-asset DCF is the right method, but the FY2037E cut-off is not reserve-derived: no reserve statement exists and no reserve life appears in the report, contrary to the commodity card's output contract. The 2031-37 tail is ~38% of PV. NAV at spot and the applied realisation haircut are also not shown.
challenges.answer: The report now states explicitly that no reserve statement exists, that the 12-year life is an explicit judgment rather than a reserve life, and treats it as a sensitised downside. The realisation ladder and price sensitivity are shown, and NAV at spot is discussed: it remains short of the quoted price on base volume.

challenges.challenge: nwc_pct 0.0 releases FY2025A operating NWC of US$4.23m into FY2026E FCFF (FCFF 7.69 vs EBITDA 4.95; 55% of that year's FCFF and ~20% of EV) and then assumes zero working capital forever, while FY2023 NWC was ~13% of revenue. The report never mentions the release.
challenges.answer: nwc_pct is set to 10%, the ratio of the operating years (FY2022 4.88/49.27, FY2024 1.75/27.25), not zero. The FY2026E release is disclosed with its delta (a source of cash) and the 10% ratio is held afterwards, so the release does not repeat; the shutdown-year 42% is explicitly discarded.

challenges.challenge: The bull narrative says the RKAB is restored toward 1.5-2.6 Mt and the claim settled at a fraction, but the model applies volume x1.1 (0.90 Mt) and keeps the full -16.5m tax bridge. Rp355 contains neither stated driver, so the reader is told the bull embeds things it does not.
challenges.answer: Bull shocks now match the narrative: volume x1.83 (0.82 -> 1.5 Mt, F16), Newcastle x1.2 and realisation x1.15, with the full tax claim still charged. The narrative no longer promises a restoration the model does not contain.

challenges.challenge: The summary says base equity of "Rp20 ... before the house's liquidity discount, which takes the published target to Rp58" - a discount cannot raise value. The engine derives 58 from probability-weighted 82 x (1-30%) = 57.6, and 0.2 x 355 = 71 of the 82 is the 20%-probability bull, so 86% of the pre-discount target is one low-probability state.
challenges.answer: Summary and investment summary now show the construction: base Rp0 after the claim, probability-weighted Rp76, 30% liquidity discount to Rp54, and the 20% bull weight that dominates it. A doubled-bull test is discussed and still leaves the target below price; the false claim that the bull state cannot reach the quoted value is removed.

challenges.challenge: The reverse DCF (implied newc 145.4) is not in the engine output or the packet and holds volume at 0.82 Mt; the report itself says the market may be pricing RKAB restoration to 1.5-2.6 Mt or a tax settlement. A single-variable solve cannot establish that the price is "paying for the war-premium spot to persist".
challenges.answer: Section 4 now shows the reverse-DCF mechanics (factor 1.43 on the FY2027E marker, implied Newcastle 168.3 versus spot 150.3), states that the solve is single-variable, and gives RKAB restoration and a tax settlement as alternative explanations; the conclusion is now explicitly conditional on base volume and the full claim.

challenges.section: 3. Financial analysis and forecasts / 5. Investment risks
challenges.challenge: "Cash was US$4.1m at the half year" is wrong: 30 June 2026 cash is US$0.04m (pack latest_bs; S0) and US$4.1m is the FY2026E forecast cash. The paragraph is about funding the US$16.5m payable, so mislabelling a forecast as an actual misstates the risk. The P/B cross-check also uses FY2025A book (0.56x) when 1H26 equity is already US$22.95m (~1.0x).
challenges.answer: Cash is now described as negligible at 30 June 2026 (the pack carries US$0.04m), removing the forecast-as-actual error; net debt is shown as a small net cash position. The P/B cross-check now uses 30 June 2026 equity (F12) and market capitalisation and states the shares are at, not below, current book before the claim.

challenges.challenge: No dilution/funding scenario. With US$0.04m cash, a US$16.5m payable and a restart needing working capital, a rights issue, placement or asset sale is plausible; share_change is 0 in all scenarios and the bear ignores dilution.
challenges.answer: The bear narrative now carries a rights issue or placement at a deep discount, and section 5 explains the model treatment: a market-price placement is per-share value-neutral, the bear is already floored at zero so dilution cannot lower it further, and no funding commitment from the controlling holders is disclosed. The unsourced claim that holders could fund the claim is removed.

challenges.challenge: The US$16.5m payable is deducted at exactly book at probability 1.0 with no provision for penalties, interest or a further assessment, even though the US$4.56m SKP shows active assessment. The bear narrative says "settled without relief" but still uses 16.5m.
challenges.answer: Sections 4 and 5 now quantify the ceiling: the booked US$16.5m plus UU KUP Article 13 administrative interest, historically 2% a month for up to 24 months (S22/F32-F33), so book value is a floor, not a cap. The bear narrative pays the sanction; the bridge stays at the booked amount to avoid charging it twice, and the report says the sanction sits on top.

challenges.challenge: The cost basis contradicts itself: it cites "~30 USD/t total at scale" and "~15 USD/t direct cost that the 2023 revenue line implies", yet FY2023 COGS alone is 33.4 / 1.5-1.8 Mt = US$19-22/t. The model's non-royalty cost at 0.82 Mt (~US$25/t) is below the FY2023 ~US$29-35/t with no source beyond the ratio argument.
challenges.answer: Section 3 rebuilds FY2023 from COGS US$33.4m plus opex US$19.4m on US$58.8m revenue over the 1.5-2.6 Mt RKAB/plan bracket (F15/F16), and states the FY2027E total cost sits inside that per-tonne range with the 33% overhead ratio; the contradictory '~15 USD/t direct' claim is removed and the below-actual cost is justified by the smaller 2026 scale.

challenges.challenge: The rendered note contains impossible/garbled figures: "US$29,856,022.2m a day" (ADTV is Rp29.9m/day), "free float of 762.0%" (actual 7.62%), "818 kt-thousand-tonne", "US$19.8m million dollars", "negative operating cash flow of negative operating cash flow", and "0.5 Mt" FY2026E vs the model's 0.45 Mt. The 30% liquidity discount itself is correctly applied under fund record (ADTV below Rp100m).
challenges.answer: Fixed the render class of errors: free float reads 7.6% (not 762%), ADTV renders IDR29.9m a day, volumes render in kt/Mt without duplicated unit words, US$ placeholders no longer stack 'million dollars', FY2026E volume renders 0.45 Mt per the model, and the double negatives were rephrased. The whole report was rendered and checked block by block.

challenges.challenge: The bridge paragraph still says "the pack's net cash position (net debt of {{fin.FY2026E.net_debt|money}})" — the FY2026E forecast line, which renders as net cash of about US$0.1m — while the engine bridge deducts the 30 June 2026 balance-sheet net debt of US$0.442m (debt US$0.482m less cash US$0.039m, S0). The prose therefore calls the company net cash and understates the deduction by US$0.54m in the paragraph that carries the whole SELL, repeating the forecast-as-actual defect raised as QC Q1 and marked accepted at round-1 C9. The published target is unaffected (the engine uses the balance-sheet figure); the valuation narrative is not.
challenges.answer: Section 4 no longer cites a forecast line as a balance-sheet fact. The bridge now reads as enterprise value of {{val.methods.dcf_life.ev|money}} less the net debt on the 30 June 2026 balance sheet — the net debt line the DCF table deducts, i.e. debt of US$0.482m less cash of US$0.039m, net US$0.442m (S0) — less the US$16.5m tax item. The paragraph says plainly that {{fin.FY2026E.net_debt}} is a forecast-year line, shows net cash, and is not the figure the bridge uses; the point that the pack's debt and cash exclude the tax liability is retained.

challenges.challenge: Section 5 calls "a negotiated settlement, a reversal or a waiver of the sanction ... the single largest upside driver and ... the core of the bull case", but the bull scenario charges the full US$16.5m claim (assumptions scenarios.bull) and the same section, the investment summary and section 4 all say a settlement at a fraction is "additional upside" not in any modelled state. Rp382 is built from RKAB restoration to 1.5 Mt, Newcastle x1.2 and realisation x1.15, not from a settlement, so the sentence misdescribes the driver hierarchy of the bull-dominated target. This is the same contradiction round-1 C6 was marked accepted on, still present in the text.
challenges.answer: Section 5 now states that the bull's core driver is restoration of the RKAB to the level the company held in 2022, that every modelled state charges the claim in full, and that a settlement at a fraction of book is upside not captured in any modelled state. The scenario config is unchanged (bull shocks volume x1.83 to 1.5 Mt, Newcastle x1.2, realisation x1.15, full claim charged), so text and model now agree, as do the summary and section 4.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull narrative (RKAB restored to 1.5-2.6 Mt, tax claim settled at a fraction) is not modelled: the shocks are volume x1.1 (0.90 Mt) and the full -16.5m bridge. The largest identified upside carries zero weight, and the reverse DCF ignores volume restoration.

missing_bear_case.note: No dilution/funding scenario despite US$0.04m cash and a US$16.5m payable; the payable is capped at book with no penalties, interest or adverse-assessment case, even though the US$4.56m SKP shows active assessment.

assumption_realism.note: Realisation 0.30 is circular (the ~0.3 Mt volume is inferred from the ratio); nwc_pct 0 releases US$4.23m into FY2026E and assumes zero working capital forever; the cost basis contradicts itself (a "~15 USD/t" direct cost vs the pack-implied US$19-22/t).

evidence_and_citations.note: F14 is dated FY2025A but its locator is a 2022 article; "exported all of its volume" is contradicted by the analyst's own F5 (40% local in 2025); "cash US$4.1m at the half year" is the FY2026E forecast (actual US$0.04m); several rendered figures are garbled.

valuation_method_fit.note: Life-of-asset DCF is the right method, but the FY2037E life is not reserve-derived (no reserve statement or reserve life), NAV at spot and the realisation-haircut table are missing, and the single-variable reverse DCF is unshown and unreproducible.

bias_and_tone.note: The summary says the liquidity discount takes Rp20 to Rp58; the engine goes 23 base -> 82 probability-weighted -> 58, with 0.2 x 355 = 71 of the 82 from the 20% bull. The target is a bull-weighted number, not the base case, and the note does not say so.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Price is keyed to Newcastle via a spot-only HBA III/newc ratio although the house card says coal realises off HBA/ICI; the 9% royalty reads d.coal.hba (112) while the grade's HBA III (45.53) sits in the 5% band. No LK effective royalty rate is cited.

conservatism_audit.note: Conservative stack not sourced: 9% royalty vs 5% on HBA III; no tax relief in any scenario; bull volume only +10% against its own narrative; newc anchor vs HBA-based realisation; payout 0; 12-year life. Each pushes the target down and each needs a source or a reversal.

calibration.note: All three BLOCK flags are answered, but the calibration justification is circular (0.30 realisation -> ~0.3 Mt -> US$10.0m revenue); FY+1 is not re-priced against a sourced volume, so the gate is documented rather than met.

signoff.notes: APPROVED (round 2) — SELL, target Rp53, TR -68.6%. L1 and L2 are answered on substance in the text. Section 4 now states that the bridge deducts the net debt on the 30 June 2026 balance sheet (debt US$0.482m less cash US$0.039m, net US$0.442m), explicitly contrasts it with the FY2026E forecast line that shows net cash, and keeps the US$16.5m tax payable as a separate negative bridge claim with the UU KUP Article 13 sanction quantified on top. Section 5 now makes restoration of the RKAB to the 2022 1.5 Mt the bull's core driver, says every modelled state charges the claim in full, and places a settlement at a fraction of book outside all modelled states, consistent with the investment summary, section 4 and the scenario table. Neither repeats the C9/C6 defect. Lint PASS (only the single-method warning, explained in section 4 and cleared as QC Q3 NOTE); QC round 2 PASS, 0 BLOCK, judge PASS, bias neutral. Batch bias check clean against the published COAL peers: ratings span BUY (AADI +29.8%, PTBA +73.2%), ADD (ITMG +19.4%), HOLD (GEMS +2.9%, BSSR -8.2%, MBAP -1.4%), REDUCE (ADMR -16.5%, BUMI -11.4%, BYAN -19.2%, IATA -22.9%) and SELL (INDY -39.9%, SMMT -46.9%), so there is no shared-cause tilt. GTBO's WACC of 10.4% sits inside the 9.9-11.4% peer range and the deck is neutral on thermal coal. Its outlier inputs are each explained where they appear: realisation 0.30 (lowest but for IATA) from the 3,000 kcal grade against HBA III, royalty 5.0% (lowest in the batch) from the PP 19/2025 sub-4,200 kcal band, which cuts against rather than adds to the bearish case, and the 0.45/0.82 Mt volumes from the 2026 RKAB and restart guidance. The target is bull-dominated (base and bear Rp0, bull Rp382 at 20%, weighted Rp76 less the 30% house liquidity discount) and the note now says so; the SELL does not depend on the weighting. No broker research, ratings, targets or consensus were used or encountered. Residual cosmetic only, for the next version: section 1 calls the pack's 94.5% insider figure consistent with the 92.4% 2021 register (a 2.1pp gap that section 5 already flags). Stage left at signoff for the Director to publish.

bias.note: Both directions remain sourced. Conservative: volume held flat at the approved 0.82 Mt RKAB ceiling through FY2037E rather than the 1.5-2.6 Mt of 2022-23 (S2/F1; the 2023 plan was never delivered), and the full US$16.5m tax claim charged at probability 1.0 in every state including the bull (S7/F10), with the UU KUP sanction additional downside (S22/F32-F33). flags.message: cannot re-price the last actual year: volume FY2025A, EBITDA FY2025A
flags.justification: FY2025A is a shutdown year (US$10.0m of revenue, nil 1H26 sales, US$1.3m of cost of goods still running, S7/F6-F7), so it is not a usable calibration base, and the archive carries no tonnage series for it: the only tonnages are the 2021 restart (107,370 t, S15/F17) and the RKAB levels (1.5 Mt in 2022, S15/F16, and 2.6 Mt planned for 2023, S11/F15). We do not infer FY2025 volume from the realisation ratio; that would be circular. The model is instead calibrated on the last full operating year, FY2023: revenue of US$58.8m and total costs of US$52.8m (S0) over the 1.5-1.8 Mt the RKAB and plan bracket imply an ASP of US$32-39/t and a total cost of US$29-35/t, and the FY2027E build (ASP 35.4 USD/t; 19 USD/t direct, 5% royalty, 33% overhead = about US$32/t) sits inside both ranges. Section 4 states the unavailability of a FY2025 re-price.

flags.message: a.volume moves +82% from FY2026E to FY2037E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The +82% step is not volume growth: FY2026E is a three-month stub because the 2026 RKAB was approved only on 25 September 2026 and mining restarted in the first half of October, with management guiding 400-500 kt for the whole of 2026 (S2/F1-F4). FY2027E is the first full year at the approved 817,900-tonne ceiling, and volume is then held flat at that ceiling through the horizon rather than assumed to grow toward the 1.5-2.6 Mt levels of 2022-23 (S11, S15/F15-F16).

flags.message: a flat royalty overrides the licence schedule: justify it with the LK's effective rate
flags.justification: No LK effective royalty rate is disclosed in the archive, so the regulation band is the sourced rate. Licence IUP and the 3,000 cal/gram product (F14) place GTBO in the PP 19/2025 up-to-4,200 kcal/kg GAR tranche (deck table coal.royalty_iup_low), and the grade's HBA III reference is US$45.53/t at the latest print — below the US$70/t first threshold — so the schedule rate is 5%, not the 9% the high-GAR HBA band would give. Flat 5% is used because the deck's HBA III has no forecast path; reading the high-GAR HBA (US$112/t) would wrongly select the 9% upper band.

flags.message: expected return -69%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Three sourced drivers produce the negative return. First, the base operating value of US$5.8m is below the US$16.50m tax payable on the 30 June 2026 balance sheet (S7/F10), a senior claim not in the pack's debt line, so the base-case equity is worth nothing after the claim. Second, the product is 3,000 cal/gram and sells at roughly 0.30x Newcastle (S11/F14 and the HBA III/Newcastle spot ratio in the deck), so the through-cycle US$105/t newc anchor gives a US$31.5/t realised price against a total cash-plus-overhead cost of about US$32/t (19 USD/t direct, 5% royalty, 33% overhead). Third, volume is capped at the 0.82 Mt RKAB (S2/F1). What today's price implies is set out in the reverse DCF: it needs newc of about US$169/t, 1.43x our FY2027E US$118/t and above the US$150 spot, i.e. a price above the war-premium spot sustained in perpetuity rather than the deck's mean-reverting through-cycle path.
